long_biography.plain_text:
Giorgio Moretti studied medicine but moved early into computing, developing software for doctors and financial markets. A venture begun in Florence became Dedalus, combining clinical systems, diagnostics and electronic records. He used acquisitions and outside capital to expand the business across Europe, including the integration of NoemaLife and later healthcare-software assets from Agfa and DXC.

Successive Ardian transactions changed Moretti's position from controlling founder to minority shareholder. In 2024 his holding company acquired 50.78% of Millennium, the primary-care software operation, while retaining just over 6% of Dedalus. He reduced his executive involvement in the larger group and kept a board seat. His operational focus moved to Millennium, returning him to the general-practice software field that shaped his earliest product work.
